title: The Bhonsles of Nagpur
subtitle: The eastern arm of Maratha power · 1739 – 1853
subject: nagpur-kingdom
intro: Raghuji Bhonsle — a distant relation of Shivaji's family — built a kingdom based at Nagpur that carried Maratha power east into Gondwana, Orissa and Bengal. After defeats by the British in 1803 and 1817 it survived as a dependent state until Lord Dalhousie annexed it in 1853.

members.name: Sabaji Bhonsle
members.note: Fights his brother Mudhoji for power; killed in battle
Rules as regent for his son Raghuji II
A child at accession; British regency until 1830

events.title: Raghuji Bhonsle at Nagpur
events.summary: Raghuji establishes himself at Nagpur and absorbs the Gond kingdom of Deogarh, building a state across central India.

events.title: Raids into Bengal
events.summary: Raghuji's armies invade Bengal repeatedly; the 'bargi' raids are long remembered there.

events.title: Orissa gained
events.summary: Alivardi Khan agrees to pay chauth and cedes the revenues of Orissa; Cuttack becomes a Bhonsle possession.

events.title: Raghuji dies; Janoji succeeds
events.summary: Raghuji dies at Nagpur. His son Janoji takes over, and a long rivalry with the Peshwas over Nagpur's independence follows.

events.title: Brothers at war
events.summary: After Janoji's death his brothers Sabaji and Mudhoji fight for control; Sabaji is killed in 1775 and Mudhoji rules as regent for his son.

events.title: Battle of Argaon
events.summary: In the Second Anglo-Maratha War Raghuji II's army is defeated by Arthur Wellesley at Argaon.

events.title: Treaty of Deogaon
events.summary: Raghuji II cedes Cuttack and Orissa to the Company and accepts a British Resident at Nagpur.

events.title: Battle of Sitabuldi
events.summary: Appasaheb, who had seized power after murdering his cousin Parsoji, attacks the British Residency and is defeated at Sitabuldi hill.

events.title: A child ruler under British regency
events.summary: Appasaheb escapes; a child, Raghuji III, is placed on the throne with a British Resident governing until 1830.

events.title: Annexed by the British
events.summary: Raghuji III dies without a son; Dalhousie refuses to recognise an adopted heir and annexes Nagpur. The palace's contents are auctioned.

events.title: Central Provinces
events.summary: Nagpur becomes the capital of the new British province of the Central Provinces.
